title: Solutions Eng — Dedicated Capacity Workshop Appendix
content:
Purpose:
This appendix collects the worked examples, calculation sketches, and action items from the 2024-09-17 Solutions Eng workshop on Dedicated Capacity sizing and autoscale strategies for customer POCs. Use as a quick reference when drafting proposals or runbooks.

Context / goals: 
- Customer archetype: enterprise product team with steady peak traffic during business hours (09:00–18:00 local), occasional spikes from batch jobs and nightly exports. Requires 99.9% availability and 95th-percentile gen latency <200ms for short-chat (<=128 tokens) routes.
- Deliverable: a recommended Dedicated capacity configuration, an autoscaling policy (preferred conservative + burst), and a GPU cost estimate with sensitivity bands.

Assumptions used in examples (explicit so they can be tweaked per-customer):
- Model: Llama-2-13B-q4 (baseline); fallback: llama-2-7B-q4 or 13B-8bit variant
- Sequence lengths: avg prompt 80 tokens, avg generated tokens 70 tokens -> avg total seq_len ~150 tokens
- Target SLO: P95 latency <=200ms; availability 99.9%
- GPU types: A100-40GB (on-prem equivalent), H100-80GB (cloud fast option)
- Throughput (empiric): A100-40GB ~ 14 tok/s for 13B single-stream low-latency, H100 ~ 22 tok/s for same model (numbers approximate; see runtime bench PR #412)
- Tokenization: assume 0.75 words/token (for cost estimate translation)
- Cost: list price proxies: A100-40GB reserved hour cost equivalent $2.75/hr (committed amortized), H100 $8.50/hr (on-demand). These are placeholders; use customer cloud pricing when available.

Quick calculation patterns (copyable into proposal):
1) Steady-state tokens/sec requirement per route
   - qps * avg_output_tokens = tokens/sec. Example: 20 qps * 70 tokens = 1400 tok/s.
2) Required GPUs (throughput-limited)
   - GPUs_needed = ceil( tokens/sec_required / effective_tok_per_sec_per_gpu )
   - Example (A100): 1400 / 14 = 100 GPUs -> clearly expensive; implies need for batching, quantization, or lower-cost model variants.
3) Latency headroom / concurrency tradeoff
   - For low-latency targets we cannot batch indefinitely. Typical continuous-batching helps but only up to a point (keep P95 <200ms). If batching increases per-token latency beyond SLO, use larger pool + smaller batch sizes or prioritize latency buckets.

Scenario sketches (concrete examples from the workshop):
A) Enterprise chat product (peak 200 qps short-chat routes)
   - Avg output 50 tokens -> tok/s = 10k
   - A100 throughput 14 tok/s -> naive GPUs = 714 -> unrealistic
   - Recommended approach: frontier steps to shrink compute needs:
     1) Use model cascade: 7B for Lightweight, 13B for Premium. Route 70% traffic to 7B (after quality verification), 30% to 13B.
     2) Enable prefix/KV cache for repeated contexts (saves ~25% tokens in some customers).
     3) Aggressive batching during peak windows with latency tiering (e.g., allow higher-latency background requests 300–500ms).
   - After cascade + 70% traffic to 7B: estimate tok/s on 13B = 3000, on 7B equivalent tok/s per GPU ~ 28 -> GPUs_13B = 214; GPUs_7B = (7000/28)=250 -> combined 464 GPUs but much cheaper per-GPU on 7B quantized. Still large; needs further caching and request shaping.

B) Analytics API (mixed batch + interactive)
   - Daytime interactive: 20 qps (avg 150 tokens) = 3k tok/s; nightly batch jobs produce bursts of large sequences (1M tokens over 10 mins).
   - Recommendation: provision modest steady pool to meet daytime (e.g., 3k/14 = 215 -> try to lower by model choice), and enable burst capacity via autoscale to cloud GPUs for nightly batch (or queue background jobs). Use spot/burst for non-SLA work.

Autoscaling policy patterns (tradeoffs and recommended defaults):
- Conservative (recommended for enterprise Dedicated):
  - Min replicas = steady-state baseline (approved commit size)
  - Scale-up: triggered by 2-min sustained queue depth > X or token backlog > Y (we use token backlog > 5M tokens as a heuristic at workshop)
  - Scale-down: cool-down 30–60 mins to avoid flapping; prefer scheduled scale-down during night once burst window ends
  - Burst pool: allow warmable preemptible nodes up to N% of committed pool (e.g., 50%) using cheaper spot/ephemeral hardware in cloud or pre-provisioned burst GPUs in Dedicated contract.
- Aggressive (lower cost for variable workloads):
  - Min replicas smaller, scale-up aggressively by CPU/GPU util + request latency signals, accept transient P95 up to 350ms for cost reductions.

Cost estimation guidance (worked examples):
- Baseline formula: monthly_cost = committed_gpus * effective_hourly_cost * 24 * 30 + burst_hours * hour_cost_burst * GPUs_burst
- Example simplified: commit 20 A100 equivalents at $2.75/hr -> 20 * 2.75 * 24 * 30 = $39,600/mo. Add burst 10 GPUs 200 hours at $4/hr = 10 * 200 * 4 = $8,000 -> total ~= $47.6k/mo.
- Per-token proxy: if steady tokens/sec = 500 tok/s -> monthly tokens = 500*3600*24*30 = 1.296B tokens. Cost per 1M tokens = (monthly_cost / (monthly_tokens/1e6)) -> $47.6k / 1296 ~= $36.7 per 1M tokens. Note: wide sensitivity to model, quantization, and batching.

Operational recommendations / runbook bullets: 
- Capacity runbook entries:
  - Preflight checklist before POC: get cloud pricing, confirm model quantization variants, estimate percent of traffic eligible for cheaper model variants, get wallet/commit approval for burst pool.
  - Alerting: token_backlog > threshold, GPU_utilization > 85% for >5m, unexpected increase in short-route P95 latency.
  - Fallbacks: automatic fallback to smaller model variant when queue depth persists >10m tokens; or fanout to multi-region to reduce load.

Open questions & workshop action items (prioritized):
1) Measure effective tok/s per GPU for our specific runtime build + quantization flags (assigned: Diego, due 2024-09-30). Need microbench for 7B/13B/30B on A100/H100 with seq_len 150 and 512.
2) Collect customer-specific profile (qps by hour, seq_len distribution, percent repeat contexts) — SE template to send to AE (assigned: Priya).
3) Prototype autoscale test harness that uses token-backlog and P95 as signals (Aarav + infra).
4) Confirm contract language with sales for burst GPUs and pre-warmed capacity billing (Marissa / legal).

Notes to self / heuristics: 
- If required GPUs > 200 in naive calc, flag for architectural changes (cascade, caching, batching).
- Always present cost bands (low/expected/high) rather than single point estimate.
- For sensitive customers, provide an option to run a 2–4 week pilot where we instrument real traffic and produce validated cost numbers before committing.

Appendix: quick-reference numbers (workshop empirical):
- A100-40GB (13B q4): ~14 tok/s (latency-optimized path)
- H100-80GB (13B q4): ~22 tok/s
- A100-40GB (7B q4): ~28 tok/s
- Approx cost proxies: A100 reserved equiv $2.75/hr, H100 on-demand $8.50/hr, spot/burst discounts vary (30–70% off)

Last thought:
Customers care less about raw GPUs and more about predictability and unit economics (cost per active user or cost per 1M tokens). Proposals that show both the engineering plan (caching, cascade, autoscale rules) and commercial levers (commit size, burst pricing, pilot to validate) perform best in conversations.
